o1.biggest_strength: Gets the money right ($27.10 first order, about $38.50 over 90 days, $38 target), runs the nurse and server Spark Ads from day 1, and phases a budget that adds to $30,000 with dollar kill and scale rules.
o1.biggest_mistake: The family and mission concepts are thin: Concept 5's hook is just 'Same as Concept 1', and few hooks use Maria's or Tasha's exact words.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Write every hook in the customers' own phrases and add a geo holdout so the day-30 call doesn't rest only on a before-and-after comparison.

o2.biggest_strength: A Monday-ready plan: no spend until the test order passes, a learning bar worked out in dollars, 12 hooks written in Maria's and Tasha's own words, and a day-30 verdict that needs two of three independent reads plus a state holdout.
o2.biggest_mistake: The day-21 release rule counts TikTok-reported cost as one of its three reads, so platform numbers can help unlock the scale budget.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the TikTok-reported read in the release rule with the holdout or blended lift, and say how many new on-feet creators to brief and when.

reason: Both plans get the numbers right, but Output 2 is the one my team could run on Monday. It catches things I'd have missed: the trend sound isn't cleared for ads, the pixel has to pass a test order before any spend, and each ad group needs a minimum budget to finish learning. It also writes the ads in my customers' words and gives me a cleaner way to judge day 30.
